body_text:
For a predicate $P(x)$ on a domain $D$, the universal statement
$\forall x\in D\,P(x)$ is true exactly when $P(a)$ is true for
every $a\in D$. To prove it one fixes an arbitrary $a\in D$ and
proves $P(a)$ without using any special property of $a$. To
refute it, one exhibits a counterexample $a\in D$ for which
$P(a)$ is false.
